findings:
## (a) SCTDA strategy, sustainability, digital products

SCTDA's September 2024 "Connected Meeting" strategy lists public-private partnership, Sharjah Airport expansion, year-round events, new destinations and marine transport, service quality, and "strategic use of AI solutions"; no numeric target was published (https://www.sharjahtourism.ae/news/sharjah-welcomes-1-057-million-hotel-guests-in-8-months-and-unveils-strategy-to-further-boost-the-tourism-sector/). At GITEX October 2024 SCTDA launched a "Sustainable Tourism AI Assistant" in 40+ languages that advises on energy, waste, and sustainable mobility, crowdsources vetted solutions, and aligns with UN Tourism's sustainability statistical framework (https://www.sharjahtourism.ae/news/sctda-unveils-sustainable-tourism-ai-assistant-in-40-languages-to-drive-sustainability-in-the-sector/). At ATM April 2025 SCTDA launched the "Visit Sharjah" brand and a four-pillar strategy: promotion, industry and facilities development, regulation and star ratings, and CSR plus community-based tourism; Al Midfa called "innovation and sustainability" the two pillars of growth (https://gulfnews.com/business/exceptional-authentic-journey-sharjah-unveils-new-tourism-vision-to-attract-visitors-with-unique-offerings-1.500111412). In April 2026 SCTDA signed an MoU with AUS at House of Wisdom, citing the 2025 hackathon as the trigger (https://sharjah24.ae/en/Articles/2026/04/09/Ma14). Earlier SCTDA digital products: 2019 "Fatima" chatbot in Arabic, English, German, Chinese, and Russian (https://labiba.ai/sa/en/news/27); 2022 SharjahVerse metaverse and "Shj AI Guide" robot (https://www.zawya.com/en/press-release/events-and-conferences/scdta-launches-sharjahverse-and-shj-ai-guide-robot-at-gitex-global-2022-jhvzdfhn). No current consumer "Visit Sharjah" app and no numeric SCTDA sustainability or 2030 visitor target were found. Shurooq (a separate authority) runs the eco side: Sharjah Collection, Dh300 million, seven retreats, 154 units, including Nomad Kalba with 20 solar cabins (https://gulfnews.com/business/tourism/for-sharjah-slow-travel-boom-pays-off-new-eco-retreat-to-launch-in-q4-25-1.500237737); Mleiha National Park, 34.2 km², Emiri Decree 16 of 2024 (https://www.wam.ae/en/article/bluqjmk-mleiha-national-park-showcases-210000-years-uae). EPAA showcased 13 reserves at the IUCN Congress, October 2025 (https://www.wam.ae/en/article/bm4uwlg-epaa-participates-iucn-world-conservation-congress).

## (b) Visitor statistics

2024 (SCTDA, 30 April 2025): about 1.6 million hotel guests, +11%; Russia 270,000+ (+18%), India 170,000+ (+6%), Europe 100,000+ (+16%), China 60,000+ (+828%); Arab share: Oman 6%, Saudi Arabia 5%, Egypt 4%, Syria 3%, Iraq 3% (https://www.sharjahtourism.ae/news/sharjah-welcomed-1-6-million-hotel-guests-in-2024-reflecting-an-11-increase/). January to August 2024: 1.057 million, occupancy 66%, Russia 21%, UAE domestic 11%, India 10%, Oman 6% (same SCTDA strategy URL above). Q1 2025: 486,000 guests (Gulf News URL above). India, January to July 2025: about 130,000, +38% (https://sharjah24.ae/en/Articles/2025/09/08/Sharjah-Tourism-Authority-wraps-up-successful-2025-India-Roadshow). Full-year 2025 (Cavendish Maxwell, June 2026): 2.1 million guests (+22%), revenue Dh780 million (+20%), occupancy 78%, ADR Dh305, average stay two nights, 102 hotels, 10,700 keys (https://gulfnews.com/business/tourism/sharjah-hotels-draw-21-million-guests-as-airport-traffic-fuels-tourism-boom-1.500576026). Forbes Middle East 2026 attributes "over 2 million, +22%, 102 hotels, $212.4 million" to SCTDA (https://www.forbesmiddleeast.com/lists/?p=88423). No SCTDA release with a 2025 source-market split was found; note that +22% to 2.1 million implies a 1.72 million base, not 1.6 million. Sharjah Airport 2025: 19.48 million passengers, +13.9% from 17.1 million (https://www.wam.ae/en/article/byc8spi-sharjah-airport-welcomes-more-than-194-million).

## (c) Key sites

Heritage: Heart of Sharjah, 35,000 m², five phases, 2025 target, on the UNESCO tentative list (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_of_Sharjah). Al Hisn Fort built 1823, demolished 1969, reopened as a 12-gallery museum on 22 April 2015 (https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/restored-al-hisn-sharjah-fort-opens-to-public-as-a-museum). Souq Al Arsah about 200 years old (https://www.thenationalnews.com/uae/old-sharjah-souq-a-look-into-yesteryear-1.426782). Bait Al Naboodah, c. 1845, pearl merchant Obaid bin Isa Al Shamsi, reopened 2018 (https://www.wam.ae/en/article/hszr6xmm-bait-naboodah-opens-after-major-restoration-work).

Culture: Museum of Islamic Civilization opened June 2008, 5,000+ artefacts (https://www.khaleejtimes.com/article/more-than-5000-artefacts-on-display-at-islamic-museum). Sharjah Art Foundation founded 2009; Biennial 16 ran 6 February to 15 June 2025 (https://www.sharjahart.org/en/press/details/sharjah-art-foundation-announces-the-dates-for-march-meeting-2025-and-more-details-on-sharjah-biennial-16-events-and-programmes). Rain Room, first permanent edition, opened 29 April 2018 in Al Majarrah (https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2018/05/01/its-not-about-rain-its-about-robots-first-permanent-rain-room-opens-in-the-uae). House of Wisdom opened 9 December 2020, Foster + Partners, 305,000 books, 200,000 digital (https://gulfnews.com/amp/story/uae%2Fsharjah-ruler-opens-unique-futuristic-library---house-of-wisdom-1.75770673).

Nature: Mleiha Archaeological Centre opened January 2016 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mleiha_Archaeological_Centre). Faya Palaeolandscape inscribed UNESCO World Heritage 11 July 2025, first desert Palaeolithic site, 200,000+ years, management plan 2024 to 2030 (https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/sharjah-faya-unesco-world-heritage-list). Buhais Geology Park opened January 2020, Hopkins Architects (https://www.dezeen.com/2020/01/22/buhais-geology-park-interpretive-centre-hopkins-architects-sharjaha/amp/). Al Hefaiyah opened 2016, 12 km², Arabian leopard (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Hefaiyah_Conservation_Centre). Khor Kalba Mangrove Centre opened April 2021 (https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/kalba-gets-another-mangrove-sanctuary); joined Wetlands Link International February 2025 (https://www.wam.ae/en/article/bi9jh78-khor-kalba-mangrove-centre-joins-wetlands-link). Wasit Wetland Centre won the 2019 Aga Khan Award (https://gulftoday.ae/News/2019/09/15/Wasit-Wetland-Centre-wins-Aga-Khan-Architecture-Award). Khorfakkan Amphitheatre opened 14 December 2020, 3,600 seats (https://gulftoday.ae/Culture/2020/12/20/Thousands-visit-newly-opened-Khorfakkan--Amphitheatre-in-Sharjah-to-watch-heroic-film). Al Noor Island opened December 2015, 45,470 m², TripAdvisor top-10 Middle East 2024 (https://gulftoday.ae/business/2024/07/11/al-noor-island-listed-among-top-10-attractions-in-the-middle-east).

Leisure: Al Qasba opened 2005 with the Eye of the Emirates, since moved to Al Montazah (https://blooloop.com/theme-park/news/eye-emirates-wheel/). Al Majaz Waterfront launched 28 March 2010 (https://sharjah24.ae/en/Articles/2024/08/14/NJ268). Sharjah Safari opened February 2022, Dh1 billion (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20220222005670/en/).

## (d) Events

Sharjah Light Festival, 15th edition, 3 to 15 February 2026, 13 sites, Light Village with 75+ national projects (https://sharjah24.ae/en/Articles/2026/02/16/a3); the 13th edition drew 1.2 million+ visitors (https://www.sharjahtourism.ae/news/12-day-sharjah-light-festival-concludes-with-an-impressive-turnout-of-over-1-2-million-visitors/). SIBF 45th: 4 to 15 November 2026, Oman guest of honour (https://www.gulftoday.ae/news/2026/07/07/45th-sharjah-international-book-fair-set-for-november-4); the 44th drew 1,400,730 visitors and 2,350 exhibitors from 118 countries (https://gulfnews.com/uae/people/sharjah-book-fair-wraps-up-with-over-14-million-visitors-from-206-countries-1.500349566). SITTF 13th: Wednesday 28 October 2026, Al Jawaher Centre; the site still shows the 12th edition theme, so confirm (https://shf.sharjahtourism.ae/). The 2025 hackathon winner was "Sharjah Quest", a gamified digital-stamp itinerary app (https://sharjah24.ae/en/Articles/2025/11/06/Innovation-Hackathon-reimagines-tourism-experience-at-AUS). Summer Promotions 2026 ran 114 days and generated Dh850 million (https://gulfnews.com/business/economy/sharjah-summer-promotions-generate-dh850-million-in-economic-returns-1.500677836).

## (e) Designations

Capital of Arab Culture 1998, Islamic Culture 2014, Arab Tourism 2015 (https://sdc.gov.ae/En/NewsDetails/304/6); WHO Healthy City, first in the region, 30 September 2015 (https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/who-declares-sharjah-as-regions-first-healthy-city); UNICEF Child Friendly City, first under 2018 criteria (https://www.childfriendlycities.org/sharjah-united-arab-emirates); World Book Capital 23 April 2019 to 22 April 2020 (https://www.ifla.org/?p=110324); Creative City of Crafts and Folk Art 2019 (https://gulfnews.com/opinion/op-eds/sharjah-is-a-unesco-designated-creative-city-of-culture-1.1572617968810); UNESCO Learning City September 2022 (https://www.wam.ae/en/article/hszrfhu3-unesco-grants-sharjah-membership-global-network); Faya World Heritage 2025.

## (f) Pain points

Heat and seasonality: August average high about 42°C (https://www.dubai-online.com/essential/sharjah-weather/); a University of Sharjah study (Al-Adab Journal, September 2024) found "weakness of tourism activity during the summer period" and recommended year-round planning (https://doi.org/10.31973/xbst4j72); flagship events cluster November to February. Short stays: two nights average (Cavendish). Crowding: Khorfakkan entrances and Corniche jam on Eid and weekends (https://gulftoday.ae/News/2023/04/22/Residents-make-most-of-Eid-holidays-with-outings-and-musical-shows-in-UAE); 90% of Sharjah commuters report jams on the Dubai road (https://gulfnews.com/uae/90-of-dubai-sharjah-commuters-hit-by-traffic-jams-new-study-finds-1.500181486). Wayfinding: the only tourist bus is Shurooq's City Sightseeing with 13 stops (https://www.thenationalnews.com/uae/sharjah-brings-in-tour-buses-1.405393); no Sharjah visitor wayfinding or satisfaction survey was found. Language: Russia 21% and China fastest growing; SCTDA's own chatbot shipped in Russian and Chinese. Dry emirate: alcohol prohibited including hotels (https://www.frommers.com/destinations/sharjah/planning-a-trip/).

claims.claim: Sharjah recorded about 1.6 million hotel guests in 2024, up 11%; Russia was first with 270,000+ (+18%), India second with 170,000+ (+6%), Europe 100,000+, China 60,000+ (+828%); Oman led Arab markets at 6% (SCTDA, 30 April 2025).

Cavendish Maxwell reports 2.1 million hotel guests in 2025 (+22%), Dh780 million revenue, 78% occupancy, ADR Dh305, average stay two nights, across 102 hotels and 10,700 keys; no SCTDA release with a 2025 source-market split was found.

SCTDA already operates a Sustainable Tourism AI Assistant in 40+ languages (launched GITEX, October 2024) advising on energy, waste, and sustainable mobility, so a pitch must position against or integrate with it rather than claim novelty for a multilingual AI guide.

Faya Palaeolandscape in Sharjah's central region was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List on 11 July 2025 as the first desert Palaeolithic site, with 200,000+ years of human record and a 2024-2030 management plan; Mleiha National Park (34.2 km²) sits within it.

SCTDA's Visit Sharjah strategy (ATM, April 2025) rests on four pillars: promotion, industry and facilities development, regulation and star ratings, and CSR plus community-based tourism; the chairman named innovation and sustainability as the two pillars of growth, and SCTDA signed an MoU with AUS in April 2026 that cites this hackathon.

A University of Sharjah study (Al-Adab Journal, September 2024) concluded that tourism activity is weak in summer because of the climate and recommended strategic planning for year-round visitor flow; the 13th SITTF, where the winner will present, is on 28 October 2026 at Al Jawaher Centre.
